title: Zombie Outbreak: Your First 5 Days of Survival

lines: Day five of the zombie apocalypse.
You've even survived your neighbor Gary.
Which, statistically speaking, should've been impossible.
[groans] Oh, you've gotta be kidding me.
And the guy outside your door?
He got bitten four days ago.
Yeah. We should probably start at the beginning.
The government tells everyone to stay indoors.
So naturally, the entire city decides to go shopping.
Correct. For once, your two remaining brain cells are working together.
Unfortunately, you've got enough food to survive approximately eleven minutes.
Welcome to the supermarket. Humanity's final demonstration of common sense.
Water. Canned food. Batteries. And something to defend yourself with.
Of course. Emotional support duck. Very important during the collapse of civilization.
Day two. The internet is dead. The streets are empty. And somebody's knocking on your door at three in the morning.
Which is rude. Even by apocalypse standards.
Hiii! It's Gary. From 4B. Can I borrow some... sugar?
A locked door. A baseball bat. And a chair. The three pillars of modern home security.
Day three. You've learned two things. Don't trust your neighbors. And never trust anyone who smiles that much while asking for sugar.
Unfortunately, things are getting worse. Because the infection isn't just affecting people.
Rats. Pigeons. Even your adorable little-
Against all reasonable expectations... the duck was useful.
Congratulations. You've lost your apartment to a nine-pound cat.
[out of breath] ...At least I've still got the duck.
Day four. Your apartment belongs to the cat. The streets belong to the infected. And your building apparently belongs to Gary.
You need somewhere safer. Fewer entrances. A clear view of the surroundings. And preferably no cats.
Good news. You can still run.
For the first time in four days... you can actually see what's happening.
Okay. Maybe don't stand that close to the edge.
One can of food. Half a bottle of water. And batteries for a flashlight you forgot to bring.
An evacuation? Tomorrow morning? Well. That's either incredibly lucky... or the worst idea anyone's had all week.
...do not approach anyone showing signs of infection... especially unusual behavior...
Day five. Your water is gone. Your food is almost gone. But there's an evacuation point a few blocks away.
All you have to do... is get out of the building.
Your entire first aid kit... is one unicorn band-aid.
That is not a cure. But at least the unicorn looks confident.
Now you've got a problem. Someone needs your help. But if that bite means what you think it means... you might be the most dangerous thing in this building.
You need a distraction. Something loud. Something completely ridiculous.
[smug, slowly] I knew you'd come in handy.
Unbelievable. The duck has now saved your life twice.
[out of breath] Thank you. Seriously. You saved my life.
Wait. What happened to your arm?
Excellent. Very convincing. You should consider a career in politics.
Wait. Gary got bitten on day one. That was four days ago. And he's still talking.
Gary? How are you still alive?
[whispers] I don't think we're turning into the same thing.
Congratulations. You survived your first five days. Now you just have to survive... whatever comes next.
